neighbours.label: a word introducing a feature in a description of a building or estate (a covered terrace, the main cloister, a western tower)
fire: The cottage has an open-plan kitchen leading to a covered veranda and a walled garden.
The abbey church consists of a nave, a chancel and a ruined cloister on the south side.
The estate includes a huge orchard, two barns and a 30-metre bell tower.
Guests reach the villa through an arched gateway into a shaded courtyard.
The cathedral has a cruciform plan with a tall spire over the crossing.
The farmhouse offers a large covered porch and a stone terrace facing west.
Behind the manor lies a sunken garden with a small chapel and a dovecote.
The castle keeps its original moat, a gatehouse and a 12th-century hall.
quiet: The article covered the strike and its effect on local schools in detail.
The committee consists of a chair, a secretary and four elected members.
The company reported a huge loss, two lawsuits and a 30 percent drop in sales.
Guests reached the conference through a long queue at the registration desk.
The plan has a clear goal with a tight budget for the coming year.
The insurance offers a large payout and a fast claims process for members.
Behind the argument lies a simple question about trust and fairness.
The team keeps its original coach, a strong defence and a loyal fan base.

notes: Card: no dominant token (' clo' x4, ' covered' x2, ' huge', ' a', ')' of the top 32); all in descriptions of churches, houses and grounds listing their parts. The - pole is the list joints (and, commas, include) of the same descriptions. Near misses keep the same words outside a building description.
